providerPicker.label: Provider
providerPicker.otherSub: another provider or your own server
providerPicker.protonNote: Proton Mail reaches other mail apps only through Proton Bridge, an app that runs on your own computer. Connect a Proton mailbox from the ohmail desktop app on the computer where Bridge runs; “{other}” here does not reach it.
providerPicker.protonNoteDesktop: Proton Mail reaches other mail apps only through Proton Bridge. Start Bridge on this computer, choose “{other}”, and type 127.0.0.1 with port 1143 for incoming mail and 1025 for outgoing mail, with the password Bridge shows, not your Proton password. ohmail then asks you to trust Bridge's own certificate.
providerPicker.need_gmail: an App Password from your Google account, with 2-Step Verification on.
providerPicker.need_microsoft: an app password, or Sign in with Microsoft where it is offered.
providerPicker.need_icloud: an app-specific password from your Apple ID.
providerPicker.need_yahoo: an app password from Yahoo's Account Security page.
providerPicker.need_fastmail: an app password with access to Mail (IMAP/SMTP).
providerPicker.need_gmx: IMAP switched on in GMX's settings, and your GMX password.
providerPicker.need_infomaniak: your mailbox's password, or an application password if two-factor authentication is on.
providerPicker.need_webde: IMAP switched on in WEB.DE's settings, and your WEB.DE password.
providerPicker.need_tonline: the e-mail password from the Telekom E-Mail Center, not your Telekom login.
providerPicker.need_bluewin: your full bluewin address and the mailbox's own password.
providerPicker.need_imap: your provider's incoming (IMAP) and outgoing (SMTP) server names, and the mailbox's password.
providerPicker.lookingUp: Looking up who hosts the mail for {domain}…
providerPicker.discoveredHosts: This domain's DNS names its mail servers: {servers}.
providerPicker.note_gmail: Gmail signs in only with an App Password, not your Google password. Turn on 2-Step Verification first, or the App Passwords page says it is not available. Give the App Password any name, then paste its 16 letters here, with or without the spaces. Some work, school and Advanced Protection accounts, and accounts that sign in with security keys only, cannot create App Passwords; ohmail cannot connect those yet: ask your administrator to allow App Passwords, or connect another address.
providerPicker.note_microsoft: ohmail connects to Microsoft over IMAP, like every other mailbox — native Exchange sync over Microsoft Graph is on the roadmap and is not shipped. When this deployment has a Microsoft application registration, you can sign in with Microsoft instead and no password is stored; that option is offered only where it is actually configured. Otherwise you need an app password, which requires security defaults to be off on the account; on some work tenants an administrator has disabled IMAP entirely, and then it cannot connect at all.
providerPicker.note_icloud: iCloud needs an app-specific password (Apple ID → Sign-In and Security). Your username is usually the full @icloud.com address, even if you sign in to Apple with a different one.
providerPicker.note_yahoo: Yahoo requires an app password generated under Account Security. The account password will not work for IMAP.
providerPicker.note_fastmail: Create an app password in Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations, scoped to “Mail (IMAP/SMTP)”. Fastmail lets you revoke it on its own later.
providerPicker.note_gmx: GMX ships with IMAP switched OFF. Turn it on first in Settings → POP3 & IMAP, then use your ordinary GMX password here.
providerPicker.note_infomaniak: Use your mailbox address and its password. If the account has two-factor authentication, create an application password in the Infomaniak Manager first.
providerPicker.note_webde: WEB.DE ships with IMAP switched off. Turn it on first under Einstellungen → POP3/IMAP Abruf, then use your ordinary WEB.DE password here. If the account has two-factor authentication, create an application-specific password for it instead.
providerPicker.note_tonline: Telekom Mail signs mail apps in with its own e-mail password, not your Telekom login password. Set one in the Telekom E-Mail Center first, then use it here with your full t-online.de address.
providerPicker.note_bluewin: Use your full bluewin address and its e-mail password, the password of the mailbox itself.
providerPicker.note_imap: A provider not listed here, or your own server. You need the IMAP host, the SMTP host, and a password for the mailbox; your provider's help pages call these “incoming” and “outgoing” servers. If your domain's mail is hosted by Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, choose Gmail or Microsoft instead.

mailboxes.unavailable: This build is not connected to an ohmail server.
mailboxes.microsoftOauthNote: Sign in with Microsoft to connect this mailbox — there is no app password to create, and ohmail never sees or stores your Microsoft password.
mailboxes.oauthOfferWhich: You'll continue to microsoft.com to sign in. Most Outlook and Microsoft 365 mailboxes connect this way; if your organization blocks the sign-in, use Connect a mailbox with an app password instead.
mailboxes.deviceOauthNote: Sign in with Microsoft to connect this mailbox. This server has no Microsoft app registration of its own, so it connects the other way Microsoft supports: it gives you a short code to enter at microsoft.com, and Microsoft sends the access straight back to this server. There is no app password to create, and your Microsoft password is never typed here.
mailboxes.deviceWaiting: Leave this page open. As soon as you approve the sign-in at Microsoft, the mailbox is connected here.
mailboxes.device_declined: The Microsoft sign-in was declined, so nothing was connected. You can start again whenever you like.
mailboxes.device_expired: That code ran out of time before it was approved, so nothing was connected. Start again to get a new one.
mailboxes.device_unconfigured: Microsoft sign-in with a code is not set up on this server. Ask your server administrator to check the configuration.
mailboxes.device_state_invalid: That Microsoft sign-in is no longer in progress. Start again to get a new code.
mailboxes.device_start_unavailable: Microsoft could not provide a sign-in code. Try again in a moment.
mailboxes.device_poll_retry: Microsoft sign-in could not be checked. This page will try again.
mailboxes.device_not_allowed: This account cannot complete that Microsoft sign-in. Start again from here.
mailboxes.device_no_refresh_token: Microsoft did not grant the access ohmail needs to keep this mailbox in sync. Ask your server administrator to check the configuration.
mailboxes.device_no_address: Microsoft did not say which mailbox to connect. Try signing in again.
mailboxes.oauthConnected: {address} is connected. The first sync starts on the next pass.
mailboxes.oauthReconnected: {address} is reconnected. Syncing resumes on the next pass.
mailboxes.oauth_admin_consent_required: Your organisation has to approve ohmail before this mailbox can be connected. An administrator can grant it — either because ohmail has not been approved for your tenant yet, or because your tenant does not let people approve apps themselves.
mailboxes.oauth_consent_declined: The Microsoft sign-in was cancelled, so nothing was connected.
mailboxes.oauth_consent_failed: Microsoft could not complete the sign-in. Try connecting again.
mailboxes.oauth_state_invalid: That Outlook connection link is no longer valid. Start again from here.
mailboxes.blocked_email_unverified: Connecting a mailbox needs a confirmed address. Open the link in the mail we sent when you signed up.
mailboxes.blocked_cannot_add: This account cannot take on another mailbox right now.
mailboxes.blocked_at_limit: Every mailbox this plan includes is already connected.
mailboxes.blocked_where: Settings → Subscription has the account's own page, where a hosted account manages this.
mailboxes.inPlace: ohmail organizes these mailboxes in place — real folders on the real server. Disconnect and the folders stay.
mailboxes.inboundQuiet: Syncing works, but the last mail to arrive here came {when}. If you expect mail in this mailbox, check for a forwarding rule at your provider — a forward without “keep a copy” diverts mail before it reaches the mailbox.
mailboxes.inboundQuietNever: Syncing works, but no mail has ever arrived here. If you expect mail in this mailbox, check for a forwarding rule at your provider — a forward without “keep a copy” diverts mail before it reaches the mailbox.
mailboxes.editIntro: Re-enter the app password to store new credentials. Leave the server fields blank to keep the ones already saved.
mailboxes.editIntro_gmail: Re-enter an App Password to store new credentials. If you changed your Google password, that ended every App Password, so create a new one. Leave the server fields blank to keep the ones already saved.
mailboxes.cancelledNothingChanged: Nothing changed. You went back before the check finished.
mailboxes.factorBody: The mailbox is connected as soon as this verifies.
mailboxes.factorBodyEdit: The new mailbox settings are saved as soon as this verifies.
mailboxes.factorBodyTakeover: This mailbox is taken over as soon as this verifies.
mailboxes.notChecked: {hasSince, select, yes {Not checked · since {since}} other {Not checked}}
mailboxes.notCheckedNoteCloud: {hasSince, select, yes {ohmail Cloud has not checked this mailbox since {since}. Nothing is lost, and its mail arrives as soon as checking runs again.} other {ohmail Cloud is not checking this mailbox right now. Nothing is lost, and its mail arrives as soon as checking runs again.}}
mailboxes.notCheckedNoteServer: {hasSince, select, yes {Your ohmail server has not checked this mailbox since {since}. Nothing is lost, and its mail arrives as soon as checking runs again.} other {Your ohmail server is not checking this mailbox right now. Nothing is lost, and its mail arrives as soon as checking runs again.}}
mailboxes.err_auth: Sync failed — the mailbox rejected the password.
mailboxes.err_connect: Sync failed — the mail server is not available.
mailboxes.err_tls: Sync failed — the mail server's certificate was refused.
mailboxes.err_timeout: Sync failed — the mail server stopped responding.
mailboxes.err_auth_local: Sync failed — the server on this computer refused the sign-in. If it is a gateway such as DavMail, finish its sign-in there, then choose Sign in again in Settings → Mailboxes.
mailboxes.err_auth_gmail: Sync failed — Google refused the password. Gmail needs an App Password, and changing your Google password ends every App Password: create a new one and sign in again.
mailboxes.err_timeout_local: Sync paused — the server on this computer did not answer in time. If it is a gateway such as DavMail, its own window says why; ohmail tries again on its own.
mailboxes.err_storage: Sync failed — ohmail could not store this mail. This one is on us.
mailboxes.err_storage_count: Sync failed — ohmail could not store {n, plural, one {one item} other {{count} items}} from your account on this computer. This one is on us.
mailboxes.err_storage_capped: Sync failed — ohmail could not store {count} items from your account on this computer, more than Sync now can retry. This one is on us.
mailboxes.err_sync: Sync failed while reading the mailbox.
mailboxes.err_unknown: Sync failed, and we could not tell why.
mailboxes.err_plaintext_refused: Sync failed — the mail server's address is no longer on your own network, so ohmail will not send your password to it unencrypted.
mailboxes.err_host_refused: Sync failed — the mail server's address is not one ohmail will connect to, so your password was not sent to it. Check the server settings in Settings → Mailboxes.
mailboxes.err_port_refused: Sync failed — the mail server is set to a port that does not carry mail, so your password was not sent to it. Change the port in Settings → Mailboxes.
mailboxes.err_credential_unreadable: Sync failed — this computer can't open the saved password, so nothing was sent to the mail server. Sign in again in Settings → Mailboxes.
mailboxes.err_credential_foreign_host: Sync failed — the saved password belongs to a different mail server, so nothing was sent. Sign in again in Settings → Mailboxes.
mailboxes.probe_auth: That mail server refused the password. If your provider requires an app-specific password, generate one there and use it here instead of your account password.
mailboxes.probe_connect: We could not reach that mail server. Check the IMAP host and port.
mailboxes.probe_tls: That mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password. Check the IMAP host, and whether that port expects TLS.
mailboxes.probe_timeout: That mail server did not answer in time. Check the IMAP host and port, then try again.
mailboxes.probe_auth_local: The server on this computer refused the sign-in. It runs here, so its own window or log says why. If it is a gateway such as DavMail, finish its sign-in there, then test again.
mailboxes.probe_auth_smtp: That outgoing (SMTP) mail server refused the password. If your provider requires an app-specific password, generate one there and use it here instead of your account password.
mailboxes.probe_connect_smtp: We could not reach that mail server. Check the SMTP host and port and try again.
mailboxes.probe_timeout_smtp: That outgoing (SMTP) mail server did not answer in time. Check the SMTP host and port, and try again.
mailboxes.probe_tls_smtp: That outgoing (SMTP) mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password. Check the SMTP host, and whether the port expects TLS.
mailboxes.probe_auth_gmail_app_password_required: Google refused your Google password: Gmail signs in only with an App Password. Turn on 2-Step Verification, then create an App Password with any name and paste its 16 letters here, with or without the spaces. Some work, school and Advanced Protection accounts, and accounts that sign in with security keys only, cannot create App Passwords; ohmail cannot connect those yet: ask your administrator to allow App Passwords, or connect another address.
mailboxes.probe_auth_gmail_invalid: Google did not accept that password. Gmail needs an App Password, not your Google password: create one and paste its 16 letters here. Changing your Google password ends every App Password, so a new one is needed after that. Some work, school and Advanced Protection accounts, and accounts that sign in with security keys only, cannot create App Passwords; ohmail cannot connect those yet: ask your administrator to allow App Passwords, or connect another address.
mailboxes.probe_auth_gmail_web_login: Google wants this sign-in confirmed in a web browser first. Sign in to Gmail in a browser once, then try again here. The password may be right.
mailboxes.probe_auth_gmail_imap_disabled: Google says IMAP is turned off for this account. An administrator turns it on in the Google Admin console; then try again. The password may be right.
mailboxes.probe_auth_microsoft: Microsoft did not accept that password. Here it takes an app password, not your account password, and only on an account whose security defaults are off; on some work accounts an administrator has turned IMAP off, and then it cannot connect this way at all.
mailboxes.probe_auth_icloud: Apple did not accept that password. iCloud Mail needs an app-specific password made under Apple ID → Sign-In and Security, not your Apple ID password. The username is usually your full @icloud.com address.
mailboxes.probe_auth_yahoo: Yahoo did not accept that password. Yahoo Mail needs an app password generated under Account Security; your Yahoo account password does not work for IMAP.
mailboxes.probe_auth_fastmail: Fastmail did not accept that password. It needs an app password with access to “Mail (IMAP/SMTP)”, created under Settings → Privacy & Security → Integrations, not your Fastmail password.
mailboxes.probe_auth_gmx: GMX refused the sign-in. If IMAP is still switched off — GMX ships that way — turn it on in Settings → POP3 & IMAP and try again; otherwise check your GMX password.
mailboxes.probe_auth_infomaniak: Infomaniak did not accept that password. Use the mailbox's own password, or an application password from the Infomaniak Manager if the account has two-factor authentication.
mailboxes.probe_auth_webde: WEB.DE refused the sign-in. If IMAP is still switched off — WEB.DE ships that way — turn it on under Einstellungen → POP3/IMAP Abruf and try again; otherwise check your WEB.DE password, or use an application-specific password if the account has two-factor authentication.
mailboxes.probe_auth_tonline: Telekom did not accept that password. Mail apps sign in with the e-mail password set in the Telekom E-Mail Center, not your Telekom login password.
mailboxes.probe_auth_bluewin: Swisscom did not accept that password. Use your full bluewin address and its e-mail password, the password of the mailbox itself.
mailboxes.probe_timeout_local: The server on this computer did not answer in time. If it is a gateway such as DavMail, finish what its own window asks for, then test again.
mailboxes.probe_connect_noport: {field, select, imap {We could not reach that mail server. Check the IMAP server name and try again. A port other than 993 or 143 goes after the name, as mail.example.com:1143.} smtp {We could not reach that outgoing (SMTP) mail server. Check the SMTP server name and try again. A port other than 465 or 587 goes after the name, as smtp.example.com:2525.} outgoing {We could not reach the outgoing (SMTP) mail server. Please try again.} other {We could not reach that mail server. Please try again.}}
mailboxes.probe_timeout_noport: {field, select, imap {That mail server did not answer in time. Check the IMAP server name and try again. A port other than 993 or 143 goes after the name, as mail.example.com:1143.} smtp {That outgoing (SMTP) mail server did not answer in time. Check the SMTP server name and try again. A port other than 465 or 587 goes after the name, as smtp.example.com:2525.} outgoing {The outgoing (SMTP) mail server did not answer in time. Please try again.} other {That mail server did not answer in time. Please try again.}}
mailboxes.probe_tls_noport: {field, select, imap {That mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password. Check the IMAP server name.} smtp {That outgoing (SMTP) mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password. Check the SMTP server name.} outgoing {The outgoing (SMTP) mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password.} other {That mail server's certificate was refused, so we stopped before sending the password.}}
mailboxes.probe_storage: We could not finish checking that mailbox. Try again.
mailboxes.probe_sync: We could not finish checking that mailbox. Try again.
mailboxes.probe_unknown: We could not finish checking that mailbox, and we could not tell why. Try again.
mailboxes.probe_tls_hostname: That server's certificate is for {certHost}, not {expectedHost}, so we stopped before sending the password. Check the {protocol} host with your provider.
mailboxes.probe_tls_hostname_suggest: That server's certificate is for {certHost}, not {expectedHost}, so we stopped before sending the password. It answers to {suggestedHost} — use that as the {protocol} host.
mailboxes.probe_tls_expired: That server's certificate has expired, so we stopped before sending the password. Ask whoever runs the server to renew it.
mailboxes.probe_tls_not_yet_valid: That server's certificate is not valid yet, so we stopped before sending the password. Check with whoever runs the server.
mailboxes.probe_tls_self_signed: That server's certificate is self-signed, which we cannot verify, so we stopped before sending the password. Ask whoever runs the server to install a certificate from a public authority.
mailboxes.probe_tls_untrusted: That server's certificate is not issued by a trusted authority, so we stopped before sending the password. Ask whoever runs the server to install a certificate from a public authority.
mailboxes.probe_tls_unavailable: That {protocol} server offers no encryption — no TLS and no STARTTLS — so we stopped before sending the password.
mailboxes.probe_tls_unavailable_public: That {protocol} server offers no encryption — no TLS and no STARTTLS — so we stopped before sending the password. It is not on your own network, and ohmail sends a password unencrypted only to a server that is.
mailboxes.probe_tls_self_signed_private: That server's certificate is self-signed, which we cannot verify, so we stopped before sending the password. The server is on your own network: whoever runs this ohmail server can make it trust the authority that signed that certificate ({variable} on the api and the organizer), or the mail server can use a certificate from a public authority.
mailboxes.probe_tls_untrusted_private: That server's certificate is not issued by a trusted authority, so we stopped before sending the password. The server is on your own network: whoever runs this ohmail server can make it trust that authority ({variable} on the api and the organizer), or the mail server can use a certificate from a public authority.
mailboxes.probe_tls_self_signed_local: The server on this computer uses its own certificate, which no authority vouches for, so we stopped before sending the password. If it is Proton Mail Bridge or another app you run here, you can trust its certificate below.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_limit_reached: This account may have {limit, plural, one {# mailbox} other {# mailboxes}} and {count} are connected. Raise the limit or disconnect a mailbox to add another.
mailboxes.refused_payment_required: This account is not currently entitled to connect a mailbox. The mailboxes already connected are kept, with all their mail.
mailboxes.refused_account_suspended: This account is suspended. No mailbox can be connected while it is; nothing already connected is deleted.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_not_permitted: This account may not connect another mailbox. The mailboxes already connected are kept, with all their mail.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_exists: This mailbox is already connected to your account. To change its password, open it in Settings rather than connecting it again.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_disabled: This mailbox is disconnected. Reconnect it before setting new credentials.
mailboxes.refused_signs_in_with_oauth: {provider, select, microsoft {This mailbox signs in with Microsoft, so it takes no password. Reconnect it from Settings → Mailboxes.} other {This mailbox signs in through its provider, so it takes no password. Reconnect it from Settings → Mailboxes.}}
mailboxes.refused_credential_needed: This mailbox has no password stored on this install, so organizing it would fail at the first connection. Enter the mailbox password to organize it here.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_config_changed: {transport, select, smtp {This mailbox's outgoing (SMTP) server settings changed while this password was being checked, so it was not stored. Try again.} other {This mailbox's server settings changed while this password was being checked, so it was not stored. Try again.}}
mailboxes.refused_same_login: this machine already has that mailbox. The server and username you entered open a mailbox that is already connected here. Use "Sign in again" on that mailbox to change its password.
mailboxes.refused_organizer_host_change: While this phone organizes this mailbox, its incoming server stays as it is. Stop organizing here, change the server, then start organizing here again.
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_host_refused: {transport, select, smtp {This mailbox's outgoing (SMTP) server is at an address that is not one this service will connect to. Check the server settings in Settings → Mailboxes.} other {This mailbox's incoming (IMAP) server is at an address that is not one this service will connect to. Check the server settings in Settings → Mailboxes.}}
mailboxes.refused_mailbox_host_plaintext: {transport, select, smtp {This mailbox's outgoing (SMTP) server's address is no longer on your own network, so ohmail will not send your password to it unencrypted.} other {This mailbox's incoming (IMAP) server's address is no longer on your own network, so ohmail will not send your password to it unencrypted.}}
mailboxes.refused_field_imap_port: imap port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
mailboxes.refused_field_smtp_port: smtp port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
mailboxes.insecureConsentLabelBoth: Incoming and outgoing mail (IMAP and SMTP) without encryption
mailboxes.insecureConsentWarning: Your password and your mail cross your network unencrypted, on every sync and every send. Anyone on that network can read them. If the server starts offering encryption, ohmail switches to it.
mailboxes.trustCertificateLabel: Trust this certificate for incoming mail (IMAP): {fingerprint}
mailboxes.trustCertificateLabelSmtp: Trust this certificate for outgoing mail (SMTP): {fingerprint}
mailboxes.trustCertificateLabelBoth: Trust this certificate for incoming and outgoing mail: {fingerprint}
mailboxes.trustCertificateNote: Only for a mail server on this computer, such as Proton Mail Bridge. Compare this fingerprint (SHA-256) with the one the server shows before you trust it. If its certificate changes, ohmail stops and asks again.
mailboxes.standDown_organized_elsewhere_local: ohmail on your own machine has claimed this mailbox. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDown_organized_elsewhere_cloud: Another ohmail Cloud install has claimed this mailbox. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDownClaimedByServer: Another ohmail server has claimed this mailbox. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDown_organized_elsewhere_mobile: A phone has claimed this mailbox, and a phone organizes only while ohmail is open on it. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDown_organized_elsewhere_unknown: Another ohmail organizer has claimed this mailbox. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDownLapsed: The install that organized this mailbox has stopped, and nothing organizes it now. This install reads it — mail arrives, search works, nothing is filed from here.
mailboxes.standDownHow: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on Cloud…” below checks who holds the mailbox and then offers to move the organizing here; the other install reads it from that point.
mailboxes.standDownHowServer: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on this server…” below checks who holds the mailbox and then offers to move the organizing here; the other install reads it from that point.
mailboxes.standDownHowLapsed: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on Cloud…” below checks the mailbox and then offers to organize it here.
mailboxes.standDownHowLapsedServer: It will not start again on its own. “Take over on this server…” below checks the mailbox and then offers to organize it here.
mailboxes.organizerHeldNamed: ohmail on {machine} is organizing this mailbox. It last checked in {when}.
mailboxes.organizerHeld: Another ohmail install is organizing this mailbox. It last checked in {when}.
mailboxes.organizerStoppedNamed: ohmail on {machine} last checked in {when} and has not since.
mailboxes.organizerStopped: Another ohmail install last checked in {when} and has not since.
mailboxes.organizerNone: No other ohmail install is organizing this mailbox.
mailboxes.organizerUnreadable: This mailbox holds an organizer claim this version cannot read.
mailboxes.organizerEffect: Taking over: Cloud starts organizing this mailbox on its next pass and removes the other install's claim. That install stops the next time it checks, and its own copy of your mail is left alone.
mailboxes.organizerEffectServer: Taking over: this server starts organizing this mailbox on its next pass and removes the other install's claim. That install stops the next time it checks, and its own copy of your mail is left alone.
mailboxes.organizerEffectLapsed: Taking over: Cloud starts organizing this mailbox on its next pass and removes any claim a stopped install left behind.
mailboxes.organizerEffectLapsedServer: Taking over: this server starts organizing this mailbox on its next pass and removes any claim a stopped install left behind.
mailboxes.organizerQueued: Cloud will start organizing this mailbox on its next pass.
mailboxes.organizerQueuedServer: This server will start organizing this mailbox on its next pass.
mailboxes.organizerAlreadyServer: This server already organizes this mailbox.
mailboxes.organizerDisconnected: This mailbox is disconnected. Reconnect it instead of taking it over.
mailboxes.superseded: An earlier entry for this address is no longer in use.
mailboxes.desktopLoading: Asking the mail engine which mailboxes this install opens…
mailboxes.desktopNoneLocal: This install has no mailbox yet — “Add mailbox” connects one.
mailboxes.desktopNoneCloud: This account has no mailbox connected yet. Connecting one happens in ohmail on the web.
mailboxes.desktopNoneServer: This account has no mailbox connected yet. Connecting one happens in the web app on {host}.
mailboxes.desktopNoneHost: No mailbox is connected on {host} yet. Connecting one happens in ohmail on {host}.
mailboxes.desktopStateStorage: Could not store {n, plural, one {one item} other {{count} items}}
mailboxes.desktopStateStoreRefused: This computer cannot store mail right now
mailboxes.desktopSetAside: {n, plural, one {One message could not be read and was set aside.} other {# messages could not be read and were set aside.}}
mailboxes.desktopRemovedClaimLeftBehind: The mailbox is removed from this computer, but the mail server would not let go of this computer's hold on it. Another device that tries to organize this mailbox will wait for that hold to lapse on its own. Nothing was deleted from the mailbox itself.
mailboxes.desktopRemovedNotCleared: This mailbox could not be cleared from this computer yet, so it has not been removed. Nothing was deleted from the mailbox itself. Remove it again to retry.
mailboxes.desktopStateSignInRefused: The mail server refused the sign-in.
mailboxes.desktopStateSignInRefused_gmail: Google refused the sign-in. Gmail needs an App Password, and changing your Google password ends every App Password: create a new one and choose Sign in again.
mailboxes.desktopStateSignInRefusedLocal: The server on this computer refused the sign-in. If it is a gateway such as DavMail, finish its sign-in there, then choose Sign in again.
mailboxes.desktopStatePlaintextRefused: The mail server's address is no longer on your own network, so ohmail will not send your password to it unencrypted.
mailboxes.desktopStateCredentialUnreadable: This computer can't open the saved password, so nothing is syncing.
mailboxes.desktopStateSignInAgain: This computer can't open the saved password. Enter it again to start syncing.
mailboxes.desktopStateCredentialForeign: The saved password belongs to a different mail server, so nothing is syncing.
mailboxes.desktopStateNeedsCredential: This mailbox needs its password again. Enter it to start syncing.
mailboxes.desktopStateSessionExpired: Your sign-in on this computer expired. Sign in again.
mailboxes.desktopStateUnknown: Can't check the mail server right now.
mailboxes.desktopStateSettingsUnreadable: ohmail can't save or read this mailbox's settings ({code}). It keeps trying.
mailboxes.desktopOrganizeHere_already_organizing: This machine already organizes that mailbox. No takeover was authorized.
mailboxes.desktopOrganizeHere_removed: That mailbox was removed from this machine. Add it again in the Desktop settings pane instead.
mailboxes.desktopOrganizeHere_no_mailbox: This machine has no mailbox for that address.
mailboxes.desktopManageOnWeb: Mailboxes are managed in ohmail on the web
mailboxes.desktopManageOnWebWhy: Connecting a mailbox or changing its password stores a mailbox password; removing one deletes the password stored for it. Your account asks for a second factor before either — a check this app cannot make. Your browser can, and is already signed in. Removing one there can also erase ohmail's copy of its mail.
mailboxes.desktopNoBrowser: This computer would not open a browser. The page is at ohmail.app.
mailboxes.desktopManageOnServer: Mailboxes are managed on your server's web app
mailboxes.desktopManageOnServerWhy: Connecting a mailbox or changing its password stores a mailbox password; removing one deletes the password stored for it. Your account on {host} asks for a second factor before either — a check this app cannot make. Its web app can, in your browser. Removing one there can also erase that server's copy of its mail.
mailboxes.desktopNoBrowserServer: This computer would not open a browser. The page is at {host}.
mailboxes.desktopHoldsCount: This computer holds {count, number} of your account's {total, number} messages. The rest stay on your account and load when you reach them in a list or open one — nothing is missing.
mailboxes.desktopCopyIsACopy: Your mail lives on your mail server. What this app keeps on this computer is a copy — you can remove it and nothing is lost from the mailbox itself.
mailboxes.removeStopsReader: This computer stops reading this mailbox. It was not organizing it, so nothing else changes there.
mailboxes.removeMailSafe: Your mail is untouched. The ohmail folders and every message stay on your mail server — removing a mailbox here deletes nothing from it.
mailboxes.removeCredential: The password ohmail stored for this mailbox is deleted.
mailboxes.removeScheduled: Scheduled sends from this mailbox are closed rather than sent. Each goes back to Drafts saying why.
mailboxes.removeCopyStays: The mail ohmail has already copied stays in your account and stops being updated. Deleting your account removes it.
mailboxes.removeCopyLocal: This computer's copy of this mailbox's mail is deleted. Your mail server keeps every message.
mailboxes.removeDraftsKept: {count, plural, one {Its # unsent draft stays in Drafts on this computer; it is on no mail server.} other {Its # unsent drafts stay in Drafts on this computer; they are on no mail server.}}
mailboxes.removeDraftsKeptLast: {count, plural, one {Its # unsent draft stays in Drafts on this computer, on no mail server, and is in Drafts again once you add a mailbox.} other {Its # unsent drafts stay in Drafts on this computer, on no mail server, and are in Drafts again once you add a mailbox.}}
mailboxes.removeReconnect: You can connect this mailbox again later.
mailboxes.factorBodyRemove: Removing a mailbox deletes the password stored for it, so your account asks for a fresh second factor first.
mailboxes.removeKeepChoice: Remove, and keep ohmail's copy of its mail
mailboxes.removeEraseChoice: Remove, and erase ohmail's copy of this mailbox's mail
mailboxes.removeEraseWhat: Your mail stays on your own mail server, which keeps the master copy. Only ohmail's copy goes, and that cannot be undone.
mailboxes.removeCopyErased: ohmail's copy of this mailbox's mail is erased from your account: its messages, its drafts and its folder list. Your mail server keeps every message.
mailboxes.removeEraseTypeLabel: To erase, type this mailbox's address
mailboxes.removeEraseMismatch: That is not this mailbox's address, so nothing was removed or erased. Type it exactly as it appears above.
mailboxes.removeErased: {address} is removed, and ohmail's copy of its mail is erased: {messages, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} and {drafts, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}. Your mail server still has every message.
mailboxes.removeErasedUnanchored: {address} is removed, and ohmail's copy of its mail is erased: {messages, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} and {drafts, plural, one {# draft} other {# drafts}}. Your mail server still has every message. {unanchored, plural, one {# draft in another mailbox keeps its text and loses its reply link.} other {# drafts in other mailboxes keep their text and lose their reply link.}}
mailboxes.factorBodyErase: Erasing ohmail's copy of a mailbox's mail cannot be undone, so your account asks for a fresh second factor first.
mailboxes.listBehind: The change is saved. The mailbox list has not been read since, so it stays hidden until it is.
mailboxes.erasingLeft: Erasing ohmail's copy — {count, plural, =0 {finishing} one {# message left} other {# messages left}}
mailboxes.readerSinceCloud: Since {since} · ohmail Cloud. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing.
mailboxes.readerSinceServer: Since {since} · another ohmail server. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing.
mailboxes.readerSinceLocal: Since {since} · {name}. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing.
mailboxes.readerSinceUnknown: Since {since}. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing.
mailboxes.readerReadsOnly: This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing.
mailboxes.readerNobodyReads: This computer reads it; it moves nothing and screens nothing until you press Organize here.
mailboxes.readerLegacyStandDown: This copy of ohmail stopped opening the mailbox when it stood down, so it is not reading it either. Organizing here again takes a restart.
mailboxes.readerHolderPhone: {name} is organizing this mailbox — a phone organizes while its app is open.
mailboxes.readerHolderPhoneUnnamed: A phone is organizing this mailbox, and only while its app is open.
mailboxes.readerHolderPhoneWhy: A phone organizes while its app is open.
mailboxes.readerHolderPhoneStopped: {name}, a phone, was organizing this mailbox. Nothing is organizing it until something claims it.
mailboxes.readerHolderPhoneStoppedUnnamed: A phone was organizing this mailbox. Nothing is organizing it until something claims it.
mailboxes.readerStopped: {name} has stopped checking in. Until something organizes this mailbox, new mail waits in the inbox.
mailboxes.readerSinceLocalHow: Since {since} · {name}. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing. To organize it here, press Organize here instead.
mailboxes.readerSinceCloudHow: Since {since} · ohmail Cloud. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing. To organize it here, press Organize here instead.
mailboxes.readerSinceServerHow: Since {since} · another ohmail server. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing. To organize it here, press Organize here instead.
mailboxes.readerSinceUnknownHow: Since {since}. This computer reads the mailbox; it moves nothing and screens nothing. To organize it here, press Organize here instead.
mailboxes.readerStoppedHow: {name} has stopped checking in. Until something organizes this mailbox, new mail waits in the inbox. To organize it here, press Organize here.
mailboxes.readerAlongHere: Got it — I'm reading along here
mailboxes.readerAlongSet: You are reading along on this computer. {name} organizes this mailbox.
mailboxes.organizeHereWhat: This asks for the mailbox; it does not take it. {name} stops organizing it on its next pass — within a minute — and goes on reading it. Your rules, the screening window and the away responder travel with the mailbox. Its copy of your mail is left alone either way.
mailboxes.organizeHereWhatLegacy: This asks for the mailbox; it does not take it. Quit and reopen ohmail and this computer starts organizing it. Its copy of your mail is left alone either way.
mailboxes.organizeHereWhatNobody: Nothing organizes this mailbox right now. Confirm, and this computer starts on its next pass — within a minute — and from then on it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.organizeHereCountermandWhat: This cancels the stop you asked for. This computer keeps organizing the mailbox and nothing hands it over.
mailboxes.organizeHereQueued: Asked for. This computer takes over on its next pass — within a minute. If {name} is still organizing the mailbox, it keeps it and this computer goes on reading.
mailboxes.organizeHereQueuedLegacy: Asked for. Quit and reopen ohmail to organize this mailbox from this computer. Until then this one stays stood down.
mailboxes.noticeStopped: {name} stopped organizing {address}. Nothing files it until something takes it over.
mailboxes.noticeStoppedUnknown: The install that organized {address} has stopped. Nothing files it until something takes it over.
mailboxes.noticeStoppedMany: {count} mailboxes are no longer being organized. Nothing files them until something takes them over.
mailboxes.noticeOtherMailboxes: {count, plural, one {# other mailbox} other {# other mailboxes}}
mailboxes.noticeDismissInactive: Couldn't dismiss it — this account is not active.
mailboxes.gapLetters: {count, plural, one {# letter arrived in {address}, and no device organized it. File it by your rules?} other {# letters arrived in {address}, and no device organized them. File them by your rules?}}
mailboxes.gapStrangers: {count, plural, one {# letter from a sender you have not decided about arrived in {address}, and no device organized it. Put it in the Screener?} other {# letters from senders you have not decided about arrived in {address}, and no device organized them. Put them in the Screener?}}
mailboxes.gapBoth: {letters, plural, one {# letter for your rules} other {# letters for your rules}} and {strangers, plural, one {# from a sender you have not decided about} other {# from senders you have not decided about}} arrived in {address}, and no device organized them. File them by your rules, and put the new senders in the Screener?
mailboxes.gapChanged: The letters changed since they were counted. The new count is shown.
mailboxes.stateReleased: You stopped organizing this here on {when}.
mailboxes.stateParked: Paused while the account was closed — organizing resumes on its own
mailboxes.stateReleasedSettingsOther: This computer's settings stayed on this computer: the mailbox holds settings from a newer ohmail this one cannot read.
mailboxes.stateReleasedSettingsUnsaved: This computer's settings could not be saved to the mailbox, so they are on this computer only.
mailboxes.oauthDecideElsewhere: For a mailbox signed in with OAuth, decisions can only be made on the install that organizes it.
mailboxes.stateOrganizingHere: This computer files this mailbox: it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.stateOrganizingHereUnreachable: This computer files this mailbox but cannot reach the mail server now. When the server answers again, it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.stateOrganizingCloud: ohmail Cloud files this mailbox, whether or not this page is open: it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.stateOrganizingServer: This server files this mailbox, whether or not this page is open: it moves mail into your folders, screens strangers and applies your rules.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingWhat: This computer stops filing this mailbox and goes on reading it. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are. Any install can take it over afterwards, including this one.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingWhatCloud: ohmail Cloud stops filing this mailbox and goes on reading it. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are. Any install can take it over afterwards, ohmail Cloud included.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingWhatServer: This server stops filing this mailbox and goes on reading it. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are. Any install can take it over afterwards, this server included.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueued: Asked for. This computer stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueuedCloud: Asked for. ohmail Cloud stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingQueuedServer: Asked for. This server stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapse: Another copy of this computer keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapseCloud: Another copy of ohmail Cloud keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapseServer: Another copy of this server keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingSiblingLapseHost: Another copy of {name} keeps organizing this mailbox until its claim lapses.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingPending: Stopping on the next pass — waiting for the server to confirm.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingNot: This computer was not organizing this mailbox.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingNotCloud: ohmail Cloud was not organizing this mailbox.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingNotServer: This server was not organizing this mailbox.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingHandBack: Hand the mailbox back — the mail stays where it is.
mailboxes.stopOrganizingHandBackWhat: On its next pass this computer goes on reading the mailbox and stops filing it: it moves nothing, screens nothing and applies none of your rules. Nothing takes the mailbox over by itself except a phone that organized it before and is open; otherwise another install has to press Organize here, or you add it to ohmail Cloud.
mailboxes.stateClaimLeftBehind: Cloud is not organizing this mailbox, but its claim is still on it. Nothing else will take the mailbox over while the claim is there.
mailboxes.stateClaimLeftBehindServer: This server is not organizing this mailbox, but its claim is still on it. Nothing else will take the mailbox over while the claim is there.
mailboxes.releaseClaim: Give up the claim, keep the mail
mailboxes.releaseClaimWhat: This takes Cloud's claim off the mailbox and changes nothing else. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are, the password is kept, and any install can take the mailbox over afterwards, including this one.
mailboxes.releaseClaimWhatServer: This takes this server's claim off the mailbox and changes nothing else. Your folders and everything in them stay where they are, the password is kept, and any install can take the mailbox over afterwards, this server included.
mailboxes.setupAgainWhy: Walks through what ohmail files, how far back it screens, and AI — with what is set now filled in. Nothing moves until you agree.
mailboxes.desktopAddWhy: This computer can open more than one. Setup asks for the server and the password, tests them, and asks how far back to screen — nothing moves until you agree.
mailboxes.removeLastDoor: This is the only mailbox on this computer, so ohmail returns to its setup screen afterwards.
mailboxes.sendingUnsettled: Receiving works. Sending is not set up: {reason} — fix the outgoing server in Settings.
mailboxes.sendingUnsettledReason_auth: the outgoing server refused that password
mailboxes.sendingUnsettledReason_connect: the outgoing server could not be reached
mailboxes.sendingUnsettledReason_tls: the connection to the outgoing server could not be secured
mailboxes.sendingUnsettledReason_timeout: the outgoing server did not answer in time
mailboxes.sendingUnsettledReason_unknown: the outgoing server refused the connection
mailboxes.desktopManageOnHostWhy: Connecting a mailbox or changing its password happens in ohmail on {host}. This computer shows what {host} holds.
mailboxes.desktopHoldsCountHost: This computer holds {count} of the {total} messages {host} holds for you. The rest loads from {host} when you reach it.
mailboxes.signInAgainWhy: Changed this mailbox's password at your provider? Give ohmail the new one here. The copy on this computer, your folders and everything ohmail has organized stay exactly where they are.
mailboxes.signInAgainWhy_gmail: Changed your Google password? That ends every App Password: create a new App Password and give it to ohmail here. The copy on this computer, your folders and everything ohmail has organized stay exactly where they are.
mailboxes.signInAgainHint: Sealed on this computer and sent only to this mailbox's own server. The server and username stay as they are.
mailboxes.signInAgainDone: Signed in. This mailbox is syncing again.
mailboxes.signInAgainAskWhy: This computer no longer has this mailbox's incoming server. Enter it once; after that the password alone signs it in.
mailboxes.signInAgainAskHint: Sealed on this computer and sent only to the server above.
mailboxes.selfCheckWhy: Compares how many messages each folder holds here and on your mail server. It only reads, and changes nothing on either side.
mailboxes.selfCheckInStep: In step with your mail server.
mailboxes.selfCheckWaiting: {count, plural, one {1 message is} other {# messages are}} still waiting to be filed on your mail server.
mailboxes.selfCheckEmpty: Nothing to compare yet: no folder of this mailbox has been read.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_timeout: Could not check this mailbox: your mail server did not answer in time.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_auth: Could not check this mailbox: your mail server refused the sign-in.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_connect: Could not check this mailbox: your mail server could not be reached.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_tls: Could not check this mailbox: the secure connection to your mail server failed.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_busy: Could not check this mailbox: it already has as many connections open as ohmail uses. Try again in a moment.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_no_login: Could not check this mailbox: no sign-in is stored for it.
mailboxes.selfCheckUnreached_other: Could not check this mailbox: your mail server could not be read.
mailboxes.selfCheckDiffers: {count, plural, one {# folder differs} other {# folders differ}} from your mail server: {list}.
mailboxes.selfCheckDiffersAndUnread: {count, plural, one {# folder differs} other {# folders differ}} from your mail server: {list}; {unread, plural, one {# folder} other {# folders}} could not be read: {unreadList}.
mailboxes.selfCheckOnlyUnread: {unread, plural, one {# folder} other {# folders}} could not be read from your mail server: {unreadList}. The others are in step.
mailboxes.selfCheckServerMore: {folder} ({count, plural, one {# more message} other {# more messages}} on the server)
mailboxes.selfCheckMirrorMore: {folder} ({count, plural, one {# more message} other {# more messages}} here)
mailboxes.selfCheckPredecessor: {folder}, News' folder before the rename ({count, plural, one {# letter} other {# letters}} not moved into News yet)
mailboxes.selfCheckFailed: The check could not run. Nothing was changed.

onboarding.resumeUnreachableBody: This page couldn't get an answer from the server, so it can't tell which step of setup you are on. Nothing was changed. Try again in a moment.
onboarding.cancelWhat: Setup closes and the app opens as it is now. Nothing is half-applied: what you agreed to stays agreed, what you did not stays off. You can run setup again from Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.cancelWhatNothingAgreed: Setup closes and the app opens as it is now. Nothing was agreed, so this mailbox is not organized. You can run setup again from Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.restartWhat: Back to the first step. Keep the mailbox you connected?
onboarding.forgetStepUp: Forgetting the mailbox needs your second factor again — the check expires a few minutes after the last one. It is still connected.
onboarding.welcomeTitle: ohmail holds first-time senders until you decide, and files everything else into folders in your own mailbox.
onboarding.welcomeLead: Setup takes a few minutes. Nothing moves until you say so.
onboarding.welcomeCloudTitle: Your email is confirmed. Now the mailbox ohmail will organize.
onboarding.vanishedTitle: That mailbox is no longer connected
onboarding.vanishedLead: Setup was opened for a mailbox this account does not hold any more. Nothing here has changed, and your other mailboxes are untouched. You can connect it again under Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.chooseTitle: Which mailbox is this setup for?
onboarding.chooseLead: More than one mailbox is connected here. Choose the one to set up; the others stay as they are.
onboarding.doorReader: This one will be connected for reading
onboarding.doorReaderWhy: {name} organizes this account's mail, so a mailbox added here reads, searches and sends — it moves nothing and screens nothing. You can move organizing here later under Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.doorReaderWhyLegacy: Another install organizes this account's mail, so a mailbox added here reads, searches and sends — it moves nothing and screens nothing. You can move organizing here later under Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.mailboxLead: The mailbox ohmail organizes, in place. Real folders on your real server; your other mail apps keep seeing everything.
onboarding.mailboxHandoffLead: You connect it on the setup page, where you pick your provider and confirm it is you.
onboarding.passwordHint: Sealed on this computer and sent only to your mail server. Never your account password where the provider offers app passwords.
onboarding.passwordHintCloud: Sent to ohmail's server and stored sealed there; used only to reach this mailbox. Revocable at your provider at any time.
onboarding.user: Username, if it is not the address
onboarding.testingLocal: Asking the server on this computer. If it signs in somewhere else first (a gateway such as DavMail), finish that there — ohmail waits up to two minutes.
onboarding.probeOk: {host} answered. Signed in as {user} · {count, plural, one {1 folder} other {# folders}}.
onboarding.sendingNotSet: Sending: not set up. This mailbox will receive mail, and nothing can be sent from it until an outgoing server is filled in.
onboarding.sendingRefused: Sending: {host} refused. Check the outgoing server and its port.
onboarding.sendingRefusedAuth: Sending: {host} refused this login. Some providers want a different username or password for sending.
onboarding.sendingRefusedTls: Sending: {host}'s certificate was refused. Check the outgoing server, and whether that port expects TLS.
onboarding.sendingRefusedNoTls: Sending: {host} offers no encryption, no TLS and no STARTTLS, so the password was not sent to it.
onboarding.probeOkDetail: Nothing has been read or moved. Continue to say what ohmail may do here.
onboarding.elsewhereLead: This mailbox already has an organizer. Two installs never organize one mailbox at once.
onboarding.elsewhereLeadStopped: The install that organized this mailbox has stopped checking in, so nothing organizes it now.
onboarding.elsewhereChoiceHereWhy: {name} stops organizing on its next pass — within a minute — and becomes a reader: it keeps its copy of your mail and moves nothing. Your rules and the away responder travel with the mailbox.
onboarding.elsewhereChoiceHereStoppedWhy: This install takes the mailbox over and starts screening new mail. There is no hand-over to wait for: {name} stopped checking in.
onboarding.elsewhereChoiceReadWhy: This install reads, searches and sends. {name} keeps organizing. You can take over later from Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.elsewhereChoiceReadStoppedWhy: This install reads, searches and sends. Nothing organizes the mailbox then: new mail waits in the inbox. You can take over later from Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.elsewhereQueued: Asked for. This install takes over on its next pass — within a minute. Continue meanwhile.
onboarding.elsewhereStepUp: Taking it over needs your second factor again — the check expires a few minutes after the last one. Nothing changed.
onboarding.consentTitle: What ohmail will do to this mailbox
onboarding.consentBody: ohmail re-arranges your existing inbox. The Ohbox is your Inbox itself, so that mail stays where it is; the rest moves into folders ohmail creates inside an ohmail folder in your mailbox: News, Receipts, Screener, Screened and Quarantine. They are ordinary IMAP folders — every other mail client sees them too, and you can leave any time with your mail exactly where it is.
onboarding.consentHistory: Mail older than the window you choose next stays in the Inbox and is listed under History. History is a view: nothing in it moves.
onboarding.consentNothingYet: Nothing moves until you agree on the next screen.
onboarding.windowTitle: How far back should ohmail screen?
onboarding.windowLead: Senders with mail inside the window go through the Screener. Older mail stays in the Inbox and is listed under History — kept, searchable, not screened.
onboarding.winAllWhy: Every sender goes through the Screener. Nothing is listed under History unscreened.
onboarding.windowLater: You can widen this later in Settings → Screener: older senders then wait in the Screener as undecided, and a decision moves the mail of theirs that waits there.
onboarding.agreeCount: {letters, plural, one {# letter} other {# letters}} from {senders, plural, one {# sender} other {# senders}} you have not decided about will wait in the Screener.
onboarding.agreeCountFloor: More than {letters, number} letters from at least {senders, plural, one {# sender} other {# senders}} you have not decided about will wait in the Screener.
onboarding.agreeCountNone: Nothing in this window comes from a sender you have not decided about.
onboarding.agreeCountSoFar: ohmail is still reading this window. So far {letters, plural, one {# letter} other {# letters}} from {senders, plural, one {# sender} other {# senders}} you have not decided about would wait in the Screener; mail it reads after you agree goes to the Screener too.
onboarding.agreeCountReading: ohmail is still reading this window and has not found a letter from a sender you have not decided about yet; mail it reads after you agree goes to the Screener too.
onboarding.windowCheckingHolder: Checking whether another computer organizes this mailbox…
onboarding.holderCheckSlow: ohmail could not check yet whether another computer organizes this mailbox, so nothing was stored. Try again in a moment.
onboarding.windowStepUp: Agreeing needs your second factor again — the check expires a few minutes after the last one. Nothing was stored.
onboarding.mailboxStepUp: Testing and connecting a mailbox need your second factor again — the check expires a few minutes after the last one. Nothing was stored.
onboarding.windowGone: That mailbox is no longer connected, so nothing was saved. Close setup, connect it again, and run setup from there.
onboarding.aiLead: A model can suggest where a first-time sender belongs and draft replies. Without one, rules do all the filing — that is a complete way to run ohmail.
onboarding.aiYesWhy: You choose where the model runs on the next screen.
onboarding.aiNoWhy: Rules only. You can turn this on later in Settings.
onboarding.aiYesCloudWhy: Runs on ohmail's servers, inside your plan's AI credits. When they run out, rules carry on.
onboarding.aiYesSelfhostWhy: Runs on the model this server's operator configured.
onboarding.providerCloudBody: Suggestions and drafts run on ohmail's servers through the Claude API, inside your plan's AI credits. A suggestion sends the sender, the subject and a short extract. A draft sends the same for the message you reply to, plus the sender and a short extract of up to 20 other messages in its thread and up to 5 matching knowledge-base notes. Where a message carries a code or a login link, the credential itself is removed before the request is built.
onboarding.providerSelfhostOn: The operator has configured a model on this server. Suggestions and drafts run through it.
onboarding.providerSelfhostOff: This server has no AI model configured. Rules do all the filing; the operator can add one later.
onboarding.pullLead: ohmail is reading the mailbox and filing what falls inside the window. You can leave this screen: the pull goes on, and the status bar shows how many messages it has read.
onboarding.counterBasis: Screened and History count this mailbox's mail on this device, not the whole mailbox.
onboarding.etaSoon: Working out how long this takes…
onboarding.pullRead: Everything counted so far is read. Finishing the first pass…
onboarding.pullScreener: Checking who is waiting in the Screener…
onboarding.eta: About {eta} left · {rate, number} messages a minute
onboarding.etaDone: Done. {screened, number} screened, {history, number} listed under History.
onboarding.pullResumed: The connection dropped and came back. The pull continues where it stopped.
onboarding.pullReconnecting: The connection to your mail server dropped. ohmail is reconnecting, and the pull goes on where it stopped.
onboarding.windowReconnecting: The connection to your mail server dropped. ohmail is reconnecting, and goes on reading this window when it is back.
onboarding.decideLead: {count, plural, one {One sender is waiting. Where should their mail go?} other {# senders are waiting. Start with this one: where should their mail go?}} The decision becomes a rule for their future mail; the ✓ half also marks the waiting mail read.
onboarding.decideLeadHere: {count, plural, one {One sender who wrote to this mailbox is waiting. Where should their mail go?} other {# senders who wrote to this mailbox are waiting. Start with this one: where should their mail go?}} The decision becomes a rule for their future mail; the ✓ half also marks the waiting mail read.
onboarding.decideLeadHereUncounted: Senders who wrote to this mailbox are waiting. Start with this one: where should their mail go? The decision becomes a rule for their future mail; the ✓ half also marks the waiting mail read.
onboarding.decideReads: News — newsletters, things to read later
onboarding.decideScreened: Screen out — filed away; their future mail follows without asking
onboarding.decideAfter: Then the Screener proper: every other waiting sender, the same verbs.
onboarding.decideAfterAccount: Then the Screener proper: {count, plural, one {the one sender waiting} other {all # senders waiting}} across your mailboxes, the same verbs.
onboarding.doneScreened: {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} screened
onboarding.doneScreenedWhy: Each decision is a rule under Settings → Rules.
onboarding.doneHistory: {count, plural, one {1 message} other {# messages}} listed under History
onboarding.doneHistoryWhy: Older than the window. Still in the Inbox — nothing there moved.
onboarding.doneWhere: News, Receipts, Screener, Screened, Quarantine — inside an ohmail folder, next to your Inbox. The Ohbox is your Inbox itself.
onboarding.doneSettings: Everything here can be changed under Settings — and setup can be run again from Settings → Mailboxes.
onboarding.doneReaderReadsWhy: Reading, searching, marking read and sending all work. It moves nothing and screens nothing — the organizer below does that.
onboarding.doneReaderReadsWhyStopped: Reading, searching, marking read and sending all work. It moves nothing and screens nothing, and the organizer below has stopped, so new mail waits in the inbox.
onboarding.doneReaderClaim: You can organize from here later
onboarding.doneReaderClaimWhy: Settings → Mailboxes has the button. Whatever organizes it then becomes a reader and keeps its copy of your mail.
onboarding.doneReaderClaimWhyStopped: Settings → Mailboxes has the button. Nothing has to hand the mailbox over first.
onboarding.doneTakeoverLands: Taking over organizing — this usually lands within a minute
onboarding.doneStartLands: Starting to organize — this usually begins within a minute
onboarding.doneTakeoverLandsWhy: Until then this computer reads the mailbox and moves nothing. There is nothing else to press.
onboarding.doneTakeoverDecidedWhy: It is a rule already. Their held mail moves when this computer starts organizing.
onboarding.doneTakeoverRefused: The takeover was refused: {name} kept organizing this mailbox.
onboarding.doneTakeoverReasked: Your decision about {name} goes to the install that kept this mailbox
onboarding.doneTakeoverReaskedWhy: This computer does not organize the mailbox, so the install that does is asked. The Screener says what it answers.
onboarding.pairLead: Scan with the phone's camera. It opens ohmail there and pairs in one step — the code works once and expires in five minutes.
onboarding.pairSameNetworkWhy: The phone reaches this computer over your own network. Off, it also works over Tailscale.
onboarding.phoneWelcome: Scan the code ohmail shows under Settings → Devices, on your computer or on the web.
onboarding.phoneBannerWhy: This phone reads the mailbox. Decisions are made where it is organized.

profileImport.title: We found your ohmail settings on this mailbox
profileImport.lede: {address} carries settings a previous ohmail saved there. They travel with the mailbox — import them into this one?
profileImport.screenerPart: {count, plural, one {# screener decision} other {# screener decisions}}
profileImport.notifyPart: {count, plural, one {# notification choice} other {# notification choices}}
profileImport.signatureReplacingPart: your signature, replacing the one on this mailbox now
profileImport.removedPart: {count, plural, one {# rule removal} other {# rule removals}}
profileImport.savedByLocal: Saved {when} by ohmail on another computer.
profileImport.willDo: Importing adds them to this account's settings and keeps every rule made only here; a rule removed there after this ohmail last organized the mailbox is removed here too. Mail this ohmail held in the Screener from senders they screen out is filed where they say; nothing else in your mail changes. Until you choose, these settings stay in the mailbox.
profileImport.routingWhileOpen: Until you answer, mail from senders these settings let through stays where it arrived; other new senders are screened as usual.
profileImport.importingSlow: This mailbox answers slowly, so ohmail finishes the import in the background. The result shows here.
profileImport.importingUnreachable: ohmail could not reach this mailbox just now. It keeps trying in the background and shows the result here.
profileImport.doneSkipped: {count, plural, one {# rule couldn't be imported.} other {# rules couldn't be imported.}}
profileImport.doneRetired: {count, plural, one {# rule removed there was removed here too.} other {# rules removed there were removed here too.}}
profileImport.doneSignatureKept: The signature you typed on this mailbox stays; the saved one was not imported.
profileImport.newerBody: {address} carries settings saved by a newer version of ohmail. Update ohmail to import them — nothing is lost in the meantime.
profileImport.savedBody: You chose Not now, so they stay in the mailbox beside the settings you make here until you choose.
profileImport.replace: Save this ohmail's settings to the mailbox
profileImport.replaceNote: Saving replaces {details} in the mailbox with this ohmail's own settings within a few minutes. While this ohmail has none of its own, the mailbox keeps them.
profileImport.replaceNoteBare: Saving replaces the settings in the mailbox with this ohmail's own within a few minutes. While this ohmail has none of its own, the mailbox keeps them.
profileImport.replacedTitle: This ohmail's settings go to the mailbox within a few minutes.
profileImport.copyUnkept: ohmail can't save a copy of your settings in {address}, so a reconnect or another device won't find them there. It keeps trying.

mailboxFilings.deletesAll: {count, plural, one {You deleted it.} other {You deleted them.}}
mailboxFilings.deletesSome: {count, plural, one {1 of them you deleted.} other {# of them you deleted.}}
mailboxFilings.unread: {count, plural, one {1 message waits} other {# messages wait}} to be filed.
mailboxFilings.retried: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing here was waiting for a retry.} one {1 message will be tried again on the next pass.} other {# messages will be tried again on the next pass.}}

mailboxFilings.failed: That did not go through. Nothing was changed.
mailboxFilings.elsewhere: Another install organizes this mailbox now. Nothing was changed.
